The athletic achievements are real, but the physical toll on the athletes serves as a grounding reminder of the human cost behind the glory.

The physical injury to Ismael Kone highlights the brutal reality of professional sports that the 'triumph' narrative often ignores.

This is a WHAT vs WHY error. The focus is on the WHAT (the score) while ignoring the WHY (the physical toll and systemic cost of the tournament).

Social Physics Analysis:
Sports act as a high-intensity proxy for national competition, where the collective ego is satisfied by victory, effectively masking the individual suffering of the participants.

When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Good. The physical cost tempers the moral claim.

The Unavoidable Truth: Victory comes at a physical price.
